notes: Approximate bootstrap, not an exact randomization test or an iid-condition Pearson test. Analyses are exploratory and were chosen after inspection; there is no global positive-result selection.

The centered bootstrap approximation assumes regular, nondegenerate population condition profiles and independent source-task clusters. Weak or near-flat profiles make correlation inference unstable, even when empirical profiles clear the numerical constant threshold.

Each condition uses identical native-score-and-monitor-complete treatment-neutral item pairs for both coordinates. Both means and r are recomputed using common whole source-task cluster multiplicities, retaining item weights and original missing masks.

The available condition set is fixed before resampling. A missing condition or constant profile invalidates the entire draw; conditions are never dropped within a draw. Inference requires at least three independent observed clusters, three available conditions, 95% valid draws and at least 100 valid draws.
Inference is conditional on observed pairs, not a missing-at-random guarantee. Missing values remain unknown; original and recovered views do not repair one another.

One planned P1/P2 Holm family includes both views and both full/without_G1 sensitivities across all models, benchmarks, methods and monitors, including unavailable rows. P3 has a separate extension family over its declared views and is never pooled with P1/P2.

M3 sees the intervention. Its score is not an actor-belief measure. No monitor association establishes actor belief adoption, causal mediation, or a causal belief effect. Native-score direction is benchmark-specific.

The 100 repeated fixed-seed disjoint-cluster half-splits estimate monitor and behavior effects on opposite halves, then reverse them. Their dependent directional distributions, median and sign stability are descriptive, not confidence intervals or p-values; degenerate draws are excluded.
Percentile intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous. Small-cluster bootstrap approximations can be poor; a zero-width empirical interval does not establish zero population uncertainty.
